title: Managed to hit release button hours before I ruined my laptop.
author: crota15
selftext:
So yeah, I finally released my game on Steam today. After years of working, I pressed the release button, took a breath, and then managed to spill my homemade protein shake all over the laptop I made the game on.

Almond milk, honey, banana, protein powder, peanut butter, and water. A truly disgusting way to go out. 

And no, I can't blame AI for this one. This was 100% my own stupidity.

Anyway, years ago I started learning game development, mostly by messing around with AI because I had no idea what I was doing. My first projects relied on it a lot, then a bit less with each new project. And now we have Sime Returns.

It's a weird little action-adventure platformer inspired by games I grew up with in the late '90s and early 2000s. I've made most of it myself, but Croatian bands and artists contributed, friends helped with voice acting, and other people chipped in along the way. AI is still part of the process, mostly because I basically had no budget to work with.

I'm not going to pretend it's perfect, and I'm not trying to convince anyone to love AI. I get why people have issues with it. I just wish more people would actually look at the game before deciding it's not worth their time because I mention AI.

Maybe it's not everyone's cup of tea. Maybe only a handful of people will play it. That's fine. The people who've played it and said something nice about it have already made the whole thing feel worthwhile.

I just wanted to make a game I could be proud of, and after years, I finally got it out there.

And somehow, I managed to press the release button before destroying my laptop. So that's a win, I guess, and a lesson for everyone *do not drink on the couch!!!*

If you want to check it out, here's the Steam page:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/4002670/Sime\_Returns/

Thanks for reading :)
